_meta: Sample (fictional person) — Emily Carter (female, born 19 July 1994, 10:15, Toronto), read as a manager. Chart figures are computed by the Minh Bao engine; the text was written for this sample. Any resemblance to a real person is coincidental.
keHoach: To get a proposal approved by Emily, lead with structure, not enthusiasm. Show who owns what, the milestones and the checkpoints, and point to a precedent or a pilot that already worked. She values method and track record, so a plan built on something proven will land far better than a bold new idea. Avoid bringing something half-formed and asking her to "figure it out together" — she wants to see that the groundwork has been done.
tinhKhi: Emily is a natural organiser who thinks before she moves, prefers proven methods and manages by goals and milestones rather than hovering. She is very good at putting the right people in the right place. Her blind spot is a strong concern for reputation and precedent, which can make her slow when a risk needs to be taken, and she tends to keep work on her own plate if she doubts others will meet her standard.
chamNoc: Chaos, last-minute changes of direction and people who don't keep their word. Anything that makes her look unprepared in front of others will cost you her trust.
coiTrong: Credibility, reliability and a standing that she earned rather than demanded. She wants her word to carry weight, and she respects people whose word does too.

nenNoi.viec: Lay out owners, milestones and checkpoints up front.

nenNoi.viec: Show that her standards are protected.
nenNoi.vidu: "Nothing goes to the client without passing the same QA you set up."

tranhNoi.vidu: "I haven't worked out the details, but I think it could be huge."

tranhNoi.viec: Changing the plan after she has signed off.
tranhNoi.vidu: "Actually, we decided to go a different way this week."

tranhNoi.viec: Putting her on the spot in a meeting.
tranhNoi.vidu: "Can you just approve it now so we can move on?"

thoiDiem: She is in her 26–35 decade cycle (Po Jun, 2.8/10), a demanding stretch, although this year has slightly more favourable stars than difficult ones (6 to 5). Proposals that reduce uncertainty and lighten her load will get the warmest reception right now.
motCau: Bring Emily a plan with a precedent, and she'll bring the authority to make it happen.
